answer: Each epoch, a randomness beacon publishes challenge words like quartz, prism, and raven, and agents must respond within minutes by weaving those words into a task-specific answer signed by their key. Because the words are unknown until the epoch opens, an attacker cannot precompute template responses for a thousand fake identities; every sybil must run real inference per identity per epoch. The cost of attack scales linearly with each extra fake agent, turning cheap identity creation into per-agent compute spending, while honest nodes pay only one small answer per epoch.
